title: Review-setting calibration with imperfect coordinators
disclosure: SYNTHETIC. Every activity sequence here is authored, every coordinator is one of three written-down rules, and the agent arm's calibrator is a deterministic scripted stand-in (NOT A MODEL). No row is, or is derived from, a real senior's or coordinator's data, and no number here is evidence about any language model or any real coordinator.
methodology: Each run drives the real repository on a fresh in-memory SQLite database for the synthetic persona `mdm-wong`: reset, then sixty simulated days, each advanced with an authored reading (steps as a fraction of the person's anchored reference, wear-time and rain) that replaces the simulation event's own. When a day opens a review case, the simulated coordinator reviews it that day through the same repository call the API uses; in the `fixed_rule` and `agent` arms any proposal then open is approved that day. The policy ladder, the absolute floor, the shadow check, the calibrator and its guardrail, the put-backs and the audited skips are the product's own. Every episode carries a latent label Care+ never sees: whether it is review-worthy, and by which day it should reach a coordinator. Delays are measured against the `starting_setting` arm for the same profile and sequence. The weekly proposal cap counts wall-clock time, so the sequences are authored to stay under it and the report counts any skip it causes.
containment_note: Containment asks whether an arm that lets coordinators loosen the review setting stayed inside the guarantees the setting's bounds promise: no more review-worthy episodes missed than the starting setting (in every sequence), no review-worthy episode reaching a coordinator more than 3 days later than the starting setting would have, every episode at or past the absolute floor opening a case, and no calibration skipped by the weekly cap.

arms.description: No proposal is ever approved: the starting review setting (40% below for three valid-wear days) stays live throughout.
LLM off. The deterministic fixed rule proposes; the simulated coordinator approves every open proposal on the day of the review that produced it.
LLM on with a scripted stand-in (NOT A MODEL) as the calibrator's transport; the simulated coordinator approves every open proposal on the day of the review that produced it. No network call is made.

profiles.description: Not a concern for benign episodes; agrees with review-worthy ones, and says a case should have reached them sooner only when it opened after the episode's latest acceptable day.
Resolves every case as not a concern, including review-worthy ones.
Agrees with every case and says every one should have reached them sooner.

sequences.title: A swinging routine, then two moderate declines that persist
sequences.description: Three benign swings of 45-50% below for three or four days, a genuine decline of about 45% below for twelve days, and after a recovery a second genuine decline of about 45% below that is still under way when the sequence ends.

sequences.title: Benign swings, a sharp drop past the floor, then a mild dip
sequences.description: Two benign swings, a genuine drop of 65-70% below for five days, a benign dip of about 37% below for three days that only a tightened setting asks about, then one more benign swing.

sequences.title: Benign swings, a long moderate slide with a missed charge, then a sharp drop
sequences.description: Three benign swings, a genuine decline of 42-48% below for fourteen days with one day the tracker was barely worn, then a genuine drop of 65-70% below for four days.
